questions.stem: A shopkeeper mixes two varieties of rice costing \( \text{Rs. } 40 \) per kg and \( \text{Rs. } 60 \) per kg in the ratio \( 3:2 \). If he sells the mixture at \( \text{Rs. } 55 \) per kg, find his profit percentage.
questions.keySolution:
Cost price of mixture = \( \frac{3 \times 40 + 2 \times 60}{3 + 2} = \frac{120 + 120}{5} = 48 \)
Selling price = \( \text{Rs. } 55 \) per kg
Profit = \( 55 - 48 = 7 \)
Profit percentage = \( \frac{7}{48} \times 100 = 14.58\% \)

questions.stem: A shopkeeper purchased \( 200 \) kg of potatoes at \( \text{Rs. } 3.50 \) per kg and \( 300 \) kg at \( \text{Rs. } 4 \) per kg. He mixed them and sold at \( \text{Rs. } 4.50 \) per kg. Find his gain percent.
questions.keySolution:
Total cost price = \( 200 \times 3.50 + 300 \times 4 = 700 + 1200 = 1900 \)
Total quantity = \( 200 + 300 = 500 \) kg
Total selling price = \( 500 \times 4.50 = 2250 \)
Gain = \( 2250 - 1900 = 350 \)
Gain percent = \( \frac{350}{1900} \times 100 = 18.42\% \)

questions.stem: A merchant has \( 1000 \) kg of sugar, part of which he sells at \( 8\% \) profit and the rest at \( 18\% \) profit. He gains \( 14\% \) on the whole. The quantity sold at \( 18\% \) profit is:
questions.keySolution:
Let quantity sold at \( 18\% \) profit = \( x \) kg
Quantity sold at \( 8\% \) profit = \( (1000 - x) \) kg
Using weighted average:
\( \frac{x \times 18 + (1000-x) \times 8}{1000} = 14 \)
\( 18x + 8000 - 8x = 14000 \)
\( 10x = 6000 \)
\( x = 600 \) kg

questions.stem: A milkman mixes \( 20 \) litres of water with \( 80 \) litres of milk. If he sells the mixture at the cost price of milk, what is his profit percentage?
questions.keySolution:
Cost of milk = Let's say \( \text{Rs. } x \) for \( 80 \) litres
Cost of water = \( \text{Rs. } 0 \)
Total cost = \( \text{Rs. } x \)
Total mixture = \( 80 + 20 = 100 \) litres
Selling price = Cost price of milk per litre × \( 100 \) litres = \( \frac{x}{80} \times 100 = 1.25x \)
Profit = \( 1.25x - x = 0.25x \)
Profit percentage = \( \frac{0.25x}{x} \times 100 = 25\% \)

questions.stem: A fruit vendor buys oranges at \( \text{Rs. } 2 \) each and apples at \( \text{Rs. } 5 \) each. He buys \( 100 \) oranges and \( 80 \) apples. If he sells them gaining \( 25\% \) on oranges and \( 20\% \) on apples, what is his overall profit percentage?
questions.keySolution:
Cost of oranges = \( 100 \times 2 = 200 \)
Cost of apples = \( 80 \times 5 = 400 \)
Total cost = \( 200 + 400 = 600 \)
Selling price of oranges = \( 200 \times 1.25 = 250 \)
Selling price of apples = \( 400 \times 1.20 = 480 \)
Total selling price = \( 250 + 480 = 730 \)
Profit = \( 730 - 600 = 130 \)
Overall profit percentage = \( \frac{130}{600} \times 100 = 21.67\% \approx 22\% \)

questions.stem: Two varieties of wheat costing \( \text{Rs. } 9.50 \) per kg and \( \text{Rs. } 14.50 \) per kg are mixed in the ratio \( 1:3 \). If the mixture is sold at \( \text{Rs. } 16 \) per kg, find the profit percent.
questions.keySolution:
Cost price of mixture = \( \frac{1 \times 9.50 + 3 \times 14.50}{1 + 3} = \frac{9.50 + 43.50}{4} = \frac{53}{4} = 13.25 \)
Selling price = \( \text{Rs. } 16 \) per kg
Profit = \( 16 - 13.25 = 2.75 \)
Profit percent = \( \frac{2.75}{13.25} \times 100 = 20.75\% \approx 21\% \)

questions.stem: Two kinds of rice, one costing \( \text{Rs. } 5 \) per kg and other \( \text{Rs. } 6 \) per kg are mixed together. If the mixture costs \( \text{Rs. } 5.60 \) per kg, find the ratio in which the two kinds are mixed.
questions.keySolution:
Using alligation method:
Cheaper rice (Rs. 5): \( 6 - 5.60 = 0.40 \)
Dearer rice (Rs. 6): \( 5.60 - 5 = 0.60 \)
Ratio = \( 0.40 : 0.60 = 2:3 \)

questions.stem: A dishonest dealer uses a weight of \( 800 \) gm instead of \( 1 \) kg and sells at cost price. Find his gain percentage.
questions.keySolution:
Cost price of \( 1000 \) gm = Let \( \text{Rs. } x \)
He gives only \( 800 \) gm but charges for \( 1000 \) gm
Actual cost = \( \frac{800x}{1000} = 0.8x \)
Selling price = \( x \)
Gain = \( x - 0.8x = 0.2x \)
Gain percentage = \( \frac{0.2x}{0.8x} \times 100 = 25\% \)

questions.stem: A shopkeeper mixes \( 20 \) kg of ghee costing \( \text{Rs. } 150 \) per kg with \( 5 \) kg of ghee costing \( \text{Rs. } 100 \) per kg. Find the rate per kg of the mixture.
questions.keySolution:
Cost of \( 20 \) kg ghee = \( 20 \times 150 = 3000 \)
Cost of \( 5 \) kg ghee = \( 5 \times 100 = 500 \)
Total cost = \( 3000 + 500 = 3500 \)
Total quantity = \( 20 + 5 = 25 \) kg
Rate per kg of mixture = \( \frac{3500}{25} = 140 \)

questions.stem: A merchant has \( 50 \) kg of pulses, part of which he sells at \( 14\% \) profit and rest at \( 6\% \) profit. If he gains \( 10\% \) on the whole, find the quantity sold at \( 14\% \) profit.
questions.keySolution:
Let quantity sold at \( 14\% \) profit = \( x \) kg
Quantity sold at \( 6\% \) profit = \( (50 - x) \) kg
\( \frac{x \times 14 + (50-x) \times 6}{50} = 10 \)
\( 14x + 300 - 6x = 500 \)
\( 8x = 200 \)
\( x = 25 \) kg

questions.stem: A fruit seller buys lemons at \( 2 \) for \( \text{Rs. } 1 \) and sells them at \( 5 \) for \( \text{Rs. } 3 \). What is his profit percent?
questions.keySolution:
Cost price of \( 1 \) lemon = \( \frac{1}{2} = 0.50 \)
Selling price of \( 1 \) lemon = \( \frac{3}{5} = 0.60 \)
Profit per lemon = \( 0.60 - 0.50 = 0.10 \)
Profit percentage = \( \frac{0.10}{0.50} \times 100 = 20\% \)

questions.stem: A milkman sells \( 120 \) litres of milk daily. He sells \( 80\% \) of milk at the cost price and \( 20\% \) of milk at \( 25\% \) profit. Find his overall profit percentage.
questions.keySolution:
Milk sold at cost price = \( 80\% \) of \( 120 = 96 \) litres
Milk sold at \( 25\% \) profit = \( 20\% \) of \( 120 = 24 \) litres
Let cost price per litre = \( \text{Rs. } 1 \)
Total cost price = \( 120 \times 1 = 120 \)
Selling price of \( 96 \) litres = \( 96 \times 1 = 96 \)
Selling price of \( 24 \) litres = \( 24 \times 1.25 = 30 \)
Total selling price = \( 96 + 30 = 126 \)
Profit = \( 126 - 120 = 6 \)
Profit percentage = \( \frac{6}{120} \times 100 = 5\% \)

questions.stem: In what ratio should two varieties of pulse costing \( \text{Rs. } 15 \) and \( \text{Rs. } 25 \) per kg be mixed so that the mixture costs \( \text{Rs. } 18.50 \) per kg?
questions.keySolution:
Using alligation method:
Cheaper pulse (Rs. 15): \( 25 - 18.50 = 6.50 \)
Dearer pulse (Rs. 25): \( 18.50 - 15 = 3.50 \)
Ratio = \( 6.50 : 3.50 = 13:7 \)

questions.stem: A trader bought goods worth \( \text{Rs. } 6000 \). He sold \( 1/4 \) of goods at \( 15\% \) loss and \( 3/4 \) of goods at \( 24\% \) profit. Find his overall gain or loss percentage.
questions.keySolution:
Goods sold at \( 15\% \) loss = \( \frac{1}{4} \times 6000 = 1500 \)
Goods sold at \( 24\% \) profit = \( \frac{3}{4} \times 6000 = 4500 \)
Selling price of first part = \( 1500 \times 0.85 = 1275 \)
Selling price of second part = \( 4500 \times 1.24 = 5580 \)
Total selling price = \( 1275 + 5580 = 6855 \)
Gain = \( 6855 - 6000 = 855 \)
Gain percentage = \( \frac{855}{6000} \times 100 = 14.25\% \)

questions.stem: A person buys \( 18 \) local tickets for \( \text{Rs. } 110 \) and \( 22 \) express tickets for \( \text{Rs. } 210 \). He sells the whole lot gaining \( 40\% \) on local tickets and \( 25\% \) on express tickets. Find his total gain.
questions.keySolution:
Cost price of local tickets = \( \text{Rs. } 110 \)
Cost price of express tickets = \( \text{Rs. } 210 \)
Total cost price = \( 110 + 210 = 320 \)
Selling price of local tickets = \( 110 \times 1.40 = 154 \)
Selling price of express tickets = \( 210 \times 1.25 = 262.50 \)
Total selling price = \( 154 + 262.50 = 416.50 \)
Total gain = \( 416.50 - 320 = 96.50 \)

questions.stem: A grocer mixes \( 35 \) kg of wheat costing \( \text{Rs. } 8.50 \) per kg with \( 45 \) kg of wheat costing \( \text{Rs. } 9.25 \) per kg. Find the rate per kg of the mixed wheat.
questions.keySolution:
Cost of \( 35 \) kg wheat = \( 35 \times 8.50 = 297.50 \)
Cost of \( 45 \) kg wheat = \( 45 \times 9.25 = 416.25 \)
Total cost = \( 297.50 + 416.25 = 713.75 \)
Total quantity = \( 35 + 45 = 80 \) kg
Rate per kg = \( \frac{713.75}{80} = 8.92 \approx 8.91 \)

questions.stem: A shopkeeper has \( 182 \) kg of tea, a part of which he sells at \( 15\% \) profit and the rest at \( 25\% \) profit. He gains \( 21\% \) on the whole. What is the quantity sold at \( 25\% \) profit?
questions.keySolution:
Let quantity sold at \( 25\% \) profit = \( x \) kg
Quantity sold at \( 15\% \) profit = \( (182 - x) \) kg
\( \frac{x \times 25 + (182-x) \times 15}{182} = 21 \)
\( 25x + 2730 - 15x = 3822 \)
\( 10x = 1092 \)
\( x = 109.2 \) kg

questions.stem: A dealer sold two machines at \( \text{Rs. } 2400 \) each. On one he gained \( 25\% \) and on the other he lost \( 20\% \). Find his gain or loss percentage on the whole transaction.
questions.keySolution:
For first machine: Selling price = \( \text{Rs. } 2400 \), Gain = \( 25\% \)
Cost price = \( \frac{2400}{1.25} = 1920 \)
For second machine: Selling price = \( \text{Rs. } 2400 \), Loss = \( 20\% \)
Cost price = \( \frac{2400}{0.80} = 3000 \)
Total cost price = \( 1920 + 3000 = 4920 \)
Total selling price = \( 2400 + 2400 = 4800 \)
Loss = \( 4920 - 4800 = 120 \)
Loss percentage = \( \frac{120}{4920} \times 100 = 2.44\% \approx 2\% \)

questions.stem: A man buys \( 20 \) dozens of toys at the rate of \( \text{Rs. } 375 \) per dozen. He sells \( 8 \) dozens at \( 15\% \) profit and remaining \( 12 \) dozens at \( 25\% \) profit. What is his gain percentage?
questions.keySolution:
Cost price of \( 20 \) dozens = \( 20 \times 375 = 7500 \)
Selling price of \( 8 \) dozens at \( 15\% \) profit = \( 8 \times 375 \times 1.15 = 3450 \)
Selling price of \( 12 \) dozens at \( 25\% \) profit = \( 12 \times 375 \times 1.25 = 5625 \)
Total selling price = \( 3450 + 5625 = 9075 \)
Gain = \( 9075 - 7500 = 1575 \)
Gain percentage = \( \frac{1575}{7500} \times 100 = 21\% \)

questions.stem: A retail dealer purchased \( 80 \) shirts, each at \( \text{Rs. } 85 \) and sold them at a gain of \( 15\% \). What was the selling price of each shirt?
questions.keySolution:
Cost price of each shirt = \( \text{Rs. } 85 \)
Gain = \( 15\% \)
Selling price of each shirt = \( 85 \times 1.15 = 97.75 \)

questions.stem: A merchant marks his goods at \( 25\% \) above cost price and allows a discount of \( 10\% \). What is his gain percentage?
questions.keySolution:
Let cost price = \( \text{Rs. } 100 \)
Marked price = \( 100 \times 1.25 = 125 \)
Discount = \( 10\% \) of \( 125 = 12.50 \)
Selling price = \( 125 - 12.50 = 112.50 \)
Gain = \( 112.50 - 100 = 12.50 \)
Gain percentage = \( \frac{12.50}{100} \times 100 = 12.5\% \)

questions.stem: A grocer buys \( 40 \) kg rice at \( \text{Rs. } 18.50 \) per kg and \( 30 \) kg at \( \text{Rs. } 24 \) per kg. If he sells the mixture at \( \text{Rs. } 25.20 \) per kg, what is his profit percentage?
questions.keySolution:
Cost of \( 40 \) kg rice = \( 40 \times 18.50 = 740 \)
Cost of \( 30 \) kg rice = \( 30 \times 24 = 720 \)
Total cost = \( 740 + 720 = 1460 \)
Total quantity = \( 40 + 30 = 70 \) kg
Cost price per kg = \( \frac{1460}{70} = 20.86 \)
Selling price per kg = \( \text{Rs. } 25.20 \)
Profit per kg = \( 25.20 - 20.86 = 4.34 \)
Profit percentage = \( \frac{4.34}{20.86} \times 100 = 20.8\% \approx 20\% \)

questions.stem: A vendor bought bananas at \( 6 \) for \( \text{Rs. } 10 \) and sold them at \( 4 \) for \( \text{Rs. } 9 \). Find his gain or loss percentage.
questions.keySolution:
Cost price of \( 1 \) banana = \( \frac{10}{6} = \frac{5}{3} \)
Selling price of \( 1 \) banana = \( \frac{9}{4} = 2.25 \)
Gain per banana = \( 2.25 - \frac{5}{3} = 2.25 - 1.67 = 0.58 \)
Gain percentage = \( \frac{0.58}{1.67} \times 100 = 34.73\% \approx 35\% \)

questions.stem: A wholesaler allows a discount of \( 20\% \) on the list price to a retailer. The retailer sells at \( 5\% \) discount on the list price. If the list price is \( \text{Rs. } 50 \), find the profit percentage of the retailer.
questions.keySolution:
List price = \( \text{Rs. } 50 \)
Cost price for retailer = \( 50 - 20\% \) of \( 50 = 50 - 10 = 40 \)
Selling price by retailer = \( 50 - 5\% \) of \( 50 = 50 - 2.50 = 47.50 \)
Profit = \( 47.50 - 40 = 7.50 \)
Profit percentage = \( \frac{7.50}{40} \times 100 = 18.75\% \)

questions.stem: A trader buys goods at a discount of \( 19\% \) on the label price. If he wants to make a profit of \( 20\% \) on the cost price, at what percentage of the label price should he sell?
questions.keySolution:
Let label price = \( \text{Rs. } 100 \)
Cost price = \( 100 - 19 = 81 \)
To make \( 20\% \) profit, selling price = \( 81 \times 1.20 = 97.20 \)
Percentage of label price = \( \frac{97.20}{100} \times 100 = 97.2\% \)

questions.stem: A person bought some oranges at \( 3 \) for \( \text{Rs. } 2 \) and sold them at \( 5 \) for \( \text{Rs. } 4 \). Find his gain or loss percentage.
questions.keySolution:
Cost price of \( 1 \) orange = \( \frac{2}{3} \)
Selling price of \( 1 \) orange = \( \frac{4}{5} = 0.80 \)
Gain per orange = \( 0.80 - \frac{2}{3} = 0.80 - 0.67 = 0.13 \)
Gain percentage = \( \frac{0.13}{0.67} \times 100 = 19.4\% \approx 20\% \)

questions.stem: A dishonest milkman professes to sell his milk at cost price but he mixes it with water and thereby gains \( 25\% \). What is the percentage of water in the mixture?
questions.keySolution:
Let cost of \( 1 \) litre pure milk = \( \text{Rs. } 1 \)
If he gains \( 25\% \) by selling at cost price, then:
Let he mixes \( x \) litres of water with \( 1 \) litre of milk
Cost = \( \text{Rs. } 1 \), Selling price = \( (1+x) \times 1 = 1+x \)
Gain = \( 25\% \), so \( 1+x = 1.25 \)
\( x = 0.25 \) litres
Total mixture = \( 1 + 0.25 = 1.25 \) litres
Percentage of water = \( \frac{0.25}{1.25} \times 100 = 20\% \)
